newsitem.title: CHINA: Hong Kong leader Tung says children are US citizens.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong leader Tung says children are US citizens.

text.p: Hong Kong leader Tung Chee-hwa said on Wednesday his three children hold American passports since they were born in the United States.

Tung, who became the first leader of Chinese-ruled Hong Kong after Britain handed over the colony to Beijing at midnight on Monday, was asked at a news conference if he or any family members had U.S. passports.
"All my three children were born in America. They all hold American passports," Tung replied, without saying whether he had ever held a foreign passport himself.
Tung was a business executive with a General Motors unit in the United States in the 1960s and 1970s when his two sons and one daughter were born.
The selection rules set by China for candidates in Hong Kong's leadership contest last December, when Tung came out on top, included a ban on foreign citizenship or right of abode.
